title: Weekend Account Load: Choosing an API Under a Tight Request Budget

steps.prompt: Every weekend an integration loads 2 million Account rows that have no related records. Existing integrations leave about 5,000 of the org's daily API requests unused. Rows that fail validation must be reported one by one while the other rows load. Which API should the job use?

options.label: One Bulk API 2.0 ingest job for the weekend load
options.rationale: Bulk API processes thousands to millions of records asynchronously, so the load costs a handful of API requests instead of thousands. The job's failed-record results list each rejected row while the other rows commit.

options.label: Composite Graph requests, each carrying a graph of 500 Account nodes
options.rationale: Each graph runs as one transaction, so a single invalid Account rolls back the other 499 in its graph instead of being reported alone.

options.label: sObject Collections calls of 200 Accounts each, sent by parallel workers
options.rationale: At 200 records per call, 2 million rows need 10,000 requests, double the 5,000 left in the daily allocation.
